items.reason: Verified at UniPoolerV2.sol:72-76 vs :501-503/:531-535. The NatSpec premise (uint112 r, balance-capped a) is false for quotePool, which feeds uint256 balanceOf and an uncapped caller a into _swapAmount. The product is checked (Solidity 0.8), so the only effect is a reverting view on absurd inputs. pool() still sizes from uint112 reserves after sync (:462-463). No asset, availability or floor impact. Low would be an overstatement; dropping it would lose a real doc defect. QA/NC is correct.

feeTo live on-chain was independently verified by validity-checker. The NatSpec conditional at :495-497 is mechanically correct: _mintFee raises totalSupply before our liquidity is computed and sync() does not trigger _mintFee, so our LP count is >= the quote and minLP stays a valid floor. Our share is value-correct (fee dilution is standard pair economics borne by all LPs pro rata, not caused by the pooler). No understatement: there is no code path where the live fee switch makes a floor unsafe. Value is as a pipeline-premise correction (MR-004 'feeTo off' is void); QA is the right channel.

items.question: Does the ycn20l24 mislabel deserve Low as an operational ledger hazard?
items.reason: Mislabel verified: commit 267660b body says 'ycn20l24: pool() syncs the pair...', and UniPoolerV2.t.sol:1604 and UniPoolerV2.fork.t.sol:126 carry the same tag. Ledger: ycn20l24 = L-24 8511fd5206 (wont-fix, dust pre-seed); the sync fix closes L-25 8ec2be7d59 (fix-pending); the canonical check closes Q-19 098396142d (fix-pending, unlabeled in the commit). I enumerated every misdirection a tag-driven closer could make: (1) L-25/Q-19 left fix-pending -> never suppressed, rescanned, fail-safe. (2) L-24 flipped wont-fix -> fixed -> both statuses are suppressed, so visibility does not drop, and a re-detection of the still-live dust pre-seed surfaces as a REGRESSION (fail-loud false alarm). (3) Because Q-19 and L-24 share a verbatim title (DEDUP-20-04 split), a title-based lookup could land on Q-19 and close it fixed, which is the correct outcome anyway. No path silently suppresses a live finding or changes on-chain behaviour, so there is no Law-1 consequence to anchor Low. The one soft risk (a reader concluding the L-24 dust pre-seed is 'fixed' and skipping the create-and-seed-atomically runbook step) is covered by MR21-08 and caps at the owner-accepted 'mild inconvenience'. Informational in the Law-2 channel is right. Note for triage: the fingerprint-only closing instruction (8ec2be7d, 09839614) is load-bearing and must be carried into the /ledger proposal text.

NatSpec at :56-61 says an unsynced donation 'would be absorbed into our swap and LP mint'. Mechanically, the router fixes amountOut from reserves, the donation only slackens swap()'s k-check and is then folded into reserves by _update, and our addLiquidity mint is computed against those inflated reserves, so the donation accrues pro rata to existing LPs and never to our mint. 'Overwhelmingly this contract's POL' is a market-structure observation, and feeTo takes ~1/6 of the k growth at the next mint/burn. The code is correct (sync before sizing, never skim). The only decision the text could distort is a knowing, voluntary protocol transfer into the pair, which is a misallocation of the protocol's own gift (externally-derived value principle), not an attacker-reachable leak. No upgrade warranted.

Story-048's 'verbatim _dispatch' clause is contradicted by the intended, safer HookNotSet guard at :356, and story-051 supersedes it without a waiver. A 'restore parity' edit would reopen L-21, but it would be caught by the pinned unit test (UniPoolerV2.t.sol:1520 block) and INV3, so the hazard is loud. Law-2 bookkeeping only; informational is right. The story-051-still-in-review/ note is correctly attached.

parkedItems.topic: Fresh DefaultDispatchHook / non-accruing hook bypasses the identity-based L-21 guard
parkedItems.reason: Guard at :356 compares identity with the immutable _defaultHook (:230). DefaultDispatchHook.onDispatch is an ungated no-op, so ANY DefaultDispatchHook instance, including another dispatcher's still-default hook, passes silently. That widens the accidental surface slightly beyond 'freshly deployed', e.g. a script that carries over `otherDispatcher.hook()` from a dispatcher still on its default. I found nothing showing such a script exists (manual-review grep of phStaging2 found no DefaultDispatchHook construction or forwarding; the realistic carry-over, BalancerPoolerV2's mint-debt hook, fails loud with OnlyDispatcher). Every bypass still needs an owner setHook to a no-accruing hook or setRatio(0). The NatSpec (:91-97) and story-051 document the opt-out, and a test pins it. Impact ceiling equals L-21's: recoverable protocol-own mint-debt under-accrual, no attacker, Low. Keeping it parked rather than filed is defensible under Law 3. It does not block proposing L-21 fixed: L-21's headline (setHook skipped or reordered) is closed.
parkedItems.humanTriageNote: Optional hardening for the owner: in _dispatch or setHook, require the hook to answer dispatcher()==address(this). DefaultDispatchHook has no dispatcher() getter, so this rejects every no-op hook, not just the constructor instance, and costs one staticcall. If the owner wants the guard to cover the 'other dispatcher's default hook' copy-paste route, this is the cheap fix.

parkedItems.topic: Deliberate quote poisoning vs L-22/L-23 wont-fix rationale
parkedItems.currentDisposition: parked against owner wont-fix L-22 a846cc40e6 / L-23 c15c71fd22
parkedItems.reason: Root cause is unchanged from L-22/L-23 (spot-derived keeper floors, POL-only exposure). Only upward poisoning (raising phUSD before the keeper quotes) hurts the zap. Downward poisoning makes the keeper buy phUSD cheaply, which benefits the pooler. Upward poisoning has to survive the quote-to-execution gap against an open arbitrage anchored by PhusdStableMinter's permissionless $1 mint. Persistence across blocks is an attacker-uncontrolled external requirement unless the attacker controls consecutive block ordering. If the attacker controls only a single block, the case collapses into the in-block sandwich L-22 explicitly accepts ('We're literally tolerating an attack of this size'). The 267660b donation lever is strictly dominated, because the donor gifts tokens to LPs who are mostly POL. Exposure stays POL-only with no user funds, at the same tier the owner accepted twice. A Medium (value leak with external requirements) was considered and rejected. The extraction requires sustained multi-block mispricing against a $1 mint arb, and the owner has already priced POL tolerance leakage at Low. Re-filing would re-raise an owner wont-fix without new impact. One honest caveat for the human: L-22's numeric bound (~0.44*t*Delta) is relative to the quote, so a poisoned quote is not t-bounded. The real cap is the attacker's carry cost against the arb anchor, not t. The parked item says this correctly and leaves the coverage question to the owner, which is the right handling.
parkedItems.humanTriageNote: Owner should explicitly confirm that L-22/L-23 cover the deliberate case. The reopen trigger is unchanged: keeper cadence becomes multi-block-latent with spot-only floors and no $1/off-chain reference bound. Keep the operational guidance: bound floors against the $1 mint price, and check balanceOf==getReserves at quote time.

items.reason: Guard is the first statement of _dispatch (:356), _defaultHook is immutable (:230), and mint reverts atomically (fail-loud on an attended permissioned path, MR21-02). The new failure mode is a liveness window between replaceDispatcher(4) and setHook. It is owner-controlled, atomic, and loses no value, so it is not Medium. The residual is MR21-01.

sync() precedes sizing (:462-464), and quotePool sizes from balances (:502), which equal post-sync reserves. New surface checked: (a) a pre-pool donation is folded in and gifted to LPs (attacker loses it); (b) a donation between quote and pool can only trip the keeper's floors (self-funded grief, fail-loud, and the donor pays); (c) sync() reverts only when balances exceed uint112, which is unreachable at sUSDS supply. Nothing reaches Medium. The NatSpec half of the plan landed imprecisely (F-02-051, informational).

Canonical check at :220-221 matches the owner-confirmed plan verbatim. Residuals are a router_ trust root (MR21-03, obvious-misconfig Law 3) and the pair-must-exist-before-deploy ordering (MR21-02, fail-loud at deploy). Neither is H/M.

This is a plan-document correction in phStaging2, and it is not a code change in this repo. 267660b neither fixes nor worsens it, and the bounded arb skim on POL is unchanged, so its informational severity stands. Correctly not classed as an INCOMPLETE FIX and not auto-closed.
